A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DITTO research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The shortened title and renumbered appendices do not prevent matching corresponding content.

before.justification: V1 reports original CMCC/CCAT experiments, algorithm ablations, sample-efficiency experiments, and a 16-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds evaluator validation, HumanEval forgetting tests, lexical analysis, and demonstration-cohesiveness results.

M1.justification: The core SFT initialization, iterative DPO updates, fixed reference policy, and comparison mixture remain unchanged. Appendix H.1 adds an optional inference procedure that prompts the general model to route queries between itself and the specialized DITTO LoRA adapter.

E1.justification: V2 adds a focused HumanEval coding-retention evaluation using one CMCC-trained adapter and evaluator-validation scenarios involving human and GPT-generated CMCC texts. The principal CMCC/CCAT writing benchmarks and 16-participant email task remain unchanged; Appendix C.1 illustrates existing train/test coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.1 adds comparisons against few-shot and SFT variants using base Mistral, reporting respective win rates of 9.4 and 10.4 against DITTO. The principal comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces evaluator validation using 950 CMCC comparisons, HumanEval pass@1 testing with and without routing, and cohesiveness ratings correlated with performance. Figure 2 extends iteration testing from 1–4 to 1–7 and negative samples from 2–10 to 2–16. These substantially expand evaluation protocols without changing the principal dataset splits or default training settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds judge-validation checks, few-shot demonstration-count and prompt-wording ablations, base-Mistral controls, lexical analysis, forgetting/routing tests, and demonstration-cohesiveness analysis. Extended hyperparameter sweeps test saturation and degradation beyond v1's ranges. The original component ablations in Table 3 are retained.

E5.justification: V1 already reports three runs and standard errors. V2 adds ANOVA and Tukey significance tests for the central benchmark and user-study comparisons, bootstrap uncertainty for evaluator accuracy, and lexical log-odds, z-scores, and p-values. No increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises DITTO from 72.1% to 68.8%, SFT from 60.1% to 55.5%, few-shot from 48.1% to 51.6%, self-prompt from 44.2% to 46.9%, and zero-shot from 25.0% to 27.3%, preserving their ranking without explaining the revisions. Tables 1 and 3 remain unchanged. Substantial new results include evaluator accuracies of 81.79 ± 2.42% and 98.8 ± 0.84%, HumanEval pass@1 of 0.13 with the adapter versus 0.31 with routing, and cohesiveness correlation R = 0.42.

T1.justification: The objectives, ranking assumptions, online-imitation derivation, Jensen inequality argument, and extrapolation lemma and proofs are retained. V1 Appendix A becomes v2 Appendix B, with citation and formatting changes rather than mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim effective personalization from fewer than ten demonstrations through online comparison generation, an online-imitation interpretation, and advantages over prompting, SFT, and self-play. The expanded abstract explains the existing procedure; the main contribution and headline claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: V2 substantially revises the limitations discussion: it uses evaluator validation to qualify self-bias concerns and replaces speculative forgetting with measured degradation and a routing remedy. It adds interpretations concerning instruction-following initialization, overfitting, lexical cliches, and demonstration cohesiveness. V1's explicit uninterpretability and evaluator-prompt-sensitivity caveats disappear.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the exact few-shot and routing prompts, candidate comparison-mixture ratios, illustrative train/test pairs, and additional study information about blinding and participant expertise. Core hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosures, and the code link remain unchanged. The added mixture-search detail does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: New citations support style-evaluation arguments and added techniques or analyses, including KTO, SimPO, HumanEval, Fightin'-Words, and LLooM. The related-work organization and positioning relative to SPIN and online imitation learning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, updates author information, expands the abstract's procedural explanation, and makes localized experimental clarifications. It separates future work and adds appendix subsections while retaining the main section sequence and most method and proof prose.

P2.justification: V2 extends Figure 2's plotted ranges, adds the prompt display and few-shot ablation in Figures 4–5 and lexical results in Table 6, and adopts ICLR formatting. Most existing displays are retained; interface screenshots are relocated and renumbered, and v1 Table 6 becomes v2 Table 7.

improvement.justification: Evaluator validation, significance tests, and quantified forgetting with a tested mitigation strengthen the empirical support and address previously untested concerns. The gain is limited by the single-adapter forgetting evaluation and an unreconciled inconsistency: the introduction retains a 23.9-point user-study advantage over few-shot prompting, whereas revised Table 2 implies 17.2 points.
